with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          # The browser download is this step's one network-bound leg. A
          # starved runner can stall it past the job budget without ever
          # erroring (2026-10-23: the install hung 40m, no test started,
          # and the same run's pub get reported an unhealthy network), so
          # each attempt is time-capped and retried — mirrors the pub-get
          # wrapper's bounded-retry shape.
          install_ok=false
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 600 npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit; then
              install_ok=true
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::playwright install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
            sleep 15
          done
          if [ "$install_ok" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::error::playwright install failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to the browser CDN/apt is unhealthy"
            exit 1
          fi
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/
  # gh-1684 AC3: the fa-extension.zip size budget gate runs at PR review
  # time — the Pages deploy went red for days because #1631's intentional
  # vendor growth only surfaced in the DEPLOY leg, after merge. Any diff
  # that can move the zip builds it here, exactly like the release leg

content.text:
EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1625: dedupe the release-event twin of a tag run. The v* tag push
  # fires the full quality gate by design (the release pipeline keys on
  # the tag and the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes — gh-1537/gh-1172);

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "PARTITIONED add-in lane" framing overstates what this test simulates**

`InMemoryFsSnapshotStore` is the same record-map fake the plain-web suite already
uses (`test/persistent_web_env_test.dart`), and origin partitioning is a
browser-level boundary that is invisible to Dart code — a pane's partitioned
IndexedDB is behaviorally identical to an unpartitioned one from the app's point
of view. So this lane does not actually simulate anything add-in-specific, and
the header docs (`test/office_addin_storage_lane_test.dart:3` "against a
PARTITIONED storage backend") plus the "add-in lane" test names promise more
than they deliver.

What the tests DO add is real value — the full `save → flush() →
PersistentWebExecutionEnv.restore` round-trip (the exact
`env_factory_stub.dart` stack) behind `SessionKeysStore` and `AppsStore`, which
no existing test covered end-to-end, plus the `restorableBootConfig` keyed
composition. Also fine: the blocked-storage failure mode ("a store that throws
on load starts clean") is already pinned at `test/persistent_web_env_test.dart:305`,
so the actual partitioning failure class is not uncovered.

Suggestion: keep the tests, reword the header/test names to claim what is
actually exercised — "persistence round-trip over the web env stack (the
add-in's boot backend)" — so a future reader doesn't assume partitioning
semantics are under test.
